Action Plan:
1. Arrange urgent same-day face-to-face review at a Babylon GP hub for full physical examination.  
2. If a hub appointment is unavailable within the next few hours, patient to self-present to the nearest Emergency Department.  
3. Anticipate need for baseline blood work (FBC, U&E, LFTs, malaria/thick film, dengue serology, CRP) and any other investigations deemed necessary after examination to rule out meningitis, dengue, malaria, and other travel-related febrile illnesses.  
4. Continue symptomatic relief with paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as required (dose/route/frequency per packet instructions; current doses not documented).  
5. Advise to seek immediate medical attention sooner if severe neck stiffness, photophobia, persistent vomiting, non-blanching rash, altered consciousness, or worsening symptoms develop before the planned review.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Severe headache for 4 days.  
• History of presenting illness:  
  – Headache began 4 days ago; persistent and “very severe.”  
  – Feels febrile but temperature not measured; feels cold at times, no rigors.  
  – Generalised muscle aches.  
  – Generalised red, itchy rash that blanches with glass test.  
  – Denies photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting, cough, earache, focal weakness, or paraesthesia.  
• Travel history: Returned from Thailand ~1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; friend who travelled with him also unwell.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic medical conditions.  
• Surgical history: None reported.  
• Medications:  
  – Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Denies drug allergies.  
• Social history: Not discussed beyond recent travel.

Objective:
(No in-person examination performed – telehealth only)  
• Patient-reported rash: diffuse, red, itchy, blanching.  
• No other objective findings or vitals available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache with fever after recent travel  
   – Assessment: Undifferentiated febrile illness; differentials include dengue fever, malaria, other arboviral infections, meningitis (viral > bacterial), viral exanthem.  
   – Investigations planned: Urgent physical examination; blood tests (FBC, U&E, LFTs, CRP, malaria screen, dengue serology ± viral PCR); consider lumbar puncture if meningitis suspected after exam.  
   – Treatment planned: Symptomatic antipyretics/analgesia; intravenous fluids/antimicrobials only if indicated after assessment.  
   – Relevant referrals: Same-day in-person GP review; possible hospital referral.

2. Generalised blanching rash  
   – Assessment: Likely viral exanthem secondary to above febrile illness; dengue still to exclude.  
   – Differential diagnosis: Allergic reaction, early meningococcal rash (currently blanching), other travel-related viral rashes.  
   – Investigations planned: As above.  
   – Treatment planned: Symptomatic (antihistamine if itch troublesome).  
   – Relevant referrals: Included in Issue 1 urgent review.

3. Generalised myalgia  
   – Assessment: Likely part of systemic febrile viral illness.  
   – Investigations planned: Included above.  
   – Treatment planned: Continue paracetamol/ibuprofen; rest, hydration.  
   – Relevant referrals: None separate from Issue 1.

Quality checks:
● Missing clinically expected elements: objective vital signs (temperature, BP, HR, RR, SpO₂); full medication reconciliation; detailed social history (alcohol, smoking).  
● Internal conflicts: Patient introduced as “John Doe,” doctor later addresses patient as “Ben” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/fillers; no inaudible sections.
